blockers.description: engine_reviews is readable with the PUBLIC publishable key. Probed 2026-09-15 with a count-only request: HTTP 200, not 401, so anon SELECT is granted. content-range '*/0' shows the table currently holds ZERO ROWS, so nothing is exposed today. The exposure is latent, not realised. It would become real on the first paid engine call, because api/review-engine.js logReview() writes per-condition notes the prompt requires to be 'grounded in the record text' (400 chars each) and finding.compliant_version, a model rewrite of the customer's passage up to 600 chars. engine-activity.html reads exactly those columns from the browser with that key. That page is noindex, absent from sitemap.xml and linked from nowhere, but the KEY is not secret: it ships in 22 pages of HTML, so the reader does not need the page.

NO VISITOR EMAIL IS STORED. bench_outcomes returns 0 email-pattern and 0 SSN-pattern hits. NO GRANT WAS ALTERED and no schema changed. Options recorded in docs/enterprise-diligence/DATABASE_ACCESS_AND_EXPOSURE_REVIEW.md.

blockers.implementation_2026_09_16: BD-02 replacement read path BUILT: api/engine-activity.js, a server-mediated endpoint returning per-condition STATUS only, reading with the service role so it survives grant revocation. It returns no finding, no note, no compliant_version, no free text, and truncates the timestamp to the hour because an exact timestamp on a low-volume endpoint is a correlation handle. engine-activity.html repointed; the three render lines for ai_function, condition_triggered and compliant_version were REMOVED, not hidden. 17 projection tests, 0 failed, including a case where the upstream row carries record text and an unexpected column, neither of which passes through. It COMPUTES and does not delete: no DELETE statement and no fetch in the module. 15 tests, 0 failed, including the no-op claim tested against the real earliest row rather than asserted. NEITHER the grant revocation NOR any deletion was performed: both are production operations. STATUS: BOARD DECIDED -> IMPLEMENTED -> TESTED. NOT production verified.
blockers.t4_decision_2026_09_16: BD-10 (T-4) DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED. engine_reviews is a MIXED table: metadata and evaluation results alongside model output derived from the customer's record. A single rule would either keep the sensitive text too long or destroy the reproducibility evidence to remove it, so the rule is FIELD-LEVEL: conditions[].note, finding.compliant_version and input_preview EXPIRE AT 90 DAYS, nulled in place; the row and its statuses, determination, overall_consistency and versions are RETAINED. The 24-month telemetry rule was expressly NOT extended by inference. Establishedrather than assumed: no research script reads this table and reproducibility reporting uses findings_history and study_runs, so redaction destroys no research evidence. BD-11 (T-11) DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED: research-data.html offered engine_reviews as a data-room export with select=*, which would have returned the notes and the rewrite to anyone holding the publishable key. A second exposure path alongside B-013A, found while deciding T-4 and latent only because the table holds zero rows. Narrowed to the activity endpoint's projection. 38 retention tests, 0 failed. Guard added, 6 mutations fail correctly. NO production redaction performed: that is a production data operation.
blockers.u3_disclosure_2026_09_16: BD-12 DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED. U-3 asked whether BD-10's 90-day expiry needed disclosing. ESTABLISHED FIRST: no public page stated ANY retention period; searched '90 days', 'retention period', 'retained for' across the estate, zero results. The pages said model output about the record 'is retained' and never said for how long, which was complete before BD-10 and incomplete after it. DECIDED: disclose BY CATEGORY, not as a bare period, because a bare '90 days' reads as the whole row being deleted, which is FALSE and worse than silence. Three categories now stated on security.html and privacy.html: model output about the record kept 90 days then removed; the evaluation record retained; the submitted record never stored at all. Red-teamed against ten possible misreadings, all clear. Guard added reading the period FROM the policy module so the page cannot drift from the code, anchored to the disclosure sentence after a page-wide version passed a mutation. DISCLOSURE IS NOT IMPLEMENTATION: production still serves the old text and no expiry has run anywhere. PRODUCTION VERIFICATION REQUIRED.
blockers.note: STRUCTURAL CLARIFICATION 2026-09-17 (BD-16), recorded here because the Round G work could be misread as having closed the A limb. THE PAGE PROJECTION IS NOT THE CONTROL. The allow-list added over engine_reviews prevents the PAGE from displaying a column and prevents silent drift; it does not protect the data. The publishable key ships in 17 HTML files by design, so anyone holding it can issue select=* against any anonymously readable table directly, whatever a page asks for. THE GRANT IS THE CONTROL, and revoking the anon SELECT on engine_reviews is the A limb of this blocker. Anyone reading the allow-list work as 'engine_reviews is protected' is reading it wrong. The same holds for B-017 and finding_responses.

blockers.description: The published API contract denies a write path the code contains. openapi.json is served on production (HTTP 200, sha256 b89e7fea904cd32db78c05625cd501abb43607c7fa5ddc7dd0fa3134c1e047d3, byte-identical to the repository) and describes exactly one path, /api/v1/review-engine. Its info.summary calls the endpoint 'Stateless' and its info.description states 'The call is stateless' and 'no data-residency or retention obligation transfers to the operator of this API'. api/v1/review-engine.js:272 calls logReview() on every authenticated request, writing a row to engine_reviews carrying conditions (per-condition note, which the prompt requires to be grounded in the record text) and finding.compliant_version (a model rewrite of the passage). One clause of the description survives strict reading: the grammatical subject of 'it is not written to any table' is record text, and record text genuinely is not written. 'The call is stateless' is a separate unqualified sentence and it is false of the code. The data-residency sentence is additionally a legal conclusion barred by Rule 8, resting on the false premise. It is the same proposition the 2026-09-15 claims sweep banned from ten HTML pages, still published in JSON.

blockers.note: PRODUCTION IS NOT CURRENTLY EXPOSED, AND THAT IS NOT A DEFENCE. AUTHENTICATED is only ever true when REVIEW_API_TOKEN is provisioned; the 401 probe establishes it is unset, so no caller reaches the model, no row can be written, and engine_reviews holds 0 rows. Production is accurate today by CONFIGURATION, exactly as B-015 was. The defect is that the contract becomes false at the moment the asset is first licensed: provisioning a token to a licensee is the single act that turns on the write path the contract denies, so the first licensee is the only person who can make this document untrue, and they are the person it was written for. Two published surfaces now disagree: privacy.html:214 (BD-12, not yet deployed) says model output about the record is kept for 90 days; openapi.json (deployed) says the call is stateless and nothing is written to any table. WHY THE GUARD SUITE MISSED IT, twice over and either miss sufficient alone: check_data_handling_claims_match_the_implementation bans the substring 'no data-residency obligation', and openapi.json reads 'no data-residency OR RETENTION obligation', which defeats containment; and the sweep iterates _html_files() only, so it never read JSON at all. Found while establishing V-9 Fact A, not by the sweep. RECLASSIFICATION NOTE 2026-09-16: the residency clause in openapi.json ALSO corrects this repository's own record. Section 4 of the counsel packet stated that statements of the form 'no data-residency obligation transfers to us' were removed rather than reworded, and treated any republication as a future contingency. That was true of the HTML surfaces and was written as though it were true of the estate. A residency statement is live on production now. Section 4 is corrected in place with its prior text preserved.

No legal conclusion concerning residency, processor obligations, licensability, or transfer has been made.

blockers.description: A promise of privacy made at the point of collection is contradicted by an anonymous SELECT grant. finding.html tells every respondent, at the moment they type into the box, 'Your response is recorded privately for the research program. It is not displayed publicly', and confirms on submit with 'Recorded privately. Thank you.' The box accepts up to 4,000 characters of free text and writes to public.finding_responses. supabase-ALL.sql grants 'for select to anon using (true)' on that table, under a comment saying it was opened 'for the data room' - which contradicts the table's own earlier comment in the SAME FILE, '(no select / update / delete policy for anon: responses stay private)'. research-data.html additionally published /rest/v1/finding_responses?select=* as a data-room export and described it, in the same row, as 'private discussion/debate responses': a page describing data as private while publishing an anonymous link to it.

finding.html promise text and the 'Recorded privately' confirmation

Narrowing the projection was expressly REJECTED rather than taken: `response` IS the sensitive column and the row existed to carry it, so the table has no public projection at all. THE REMAINING HALF IS A PRODUCTION OPERATION AND CANNOT BE DONE FROM HERE: the anon SELECT grant on public.finding_responses must be revoked. DEPENDENCY CORRECTED 2026-09-18: prior text read 'queued behind B-001 alongside the B-013A revocation'. blockers.note: WHAT IS ESTABLISHED AND WHAT IS NOT. ESTABLISHED FROM REPOSITORY EVIDENCE: the promise, the grant, and the published export link all exist and contradict each other. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any response rows exist and are actually retrievable by an anonymous caller. A direct read of the production table was attempted and correctly DENIED by the execution environment's production-read control, so the live row count is PRODUCTION VERIFICATION REQUIRED and is not inferred. The remediation does not depend on the count: a privacy promise contradicted by a grant is a defect whether or not anyone has yet typed into the box. SCOPE NOTE, so this is not over-read: interaction_events was examined in the same pass and is a WEAKER case, not this one. Its collecting pages promise 'No free text and no identifying information are collected' and 'aggregated without individual attribution', and select=* over a payload jsonb is consistent with that promise. The enforcement of 'no free text' lives in the client code that builds the payload rather than in the schema, which is a separate and lesser matter recorded as X-1 rather than folded in here.

_next_action_by_vocabulary_2026_09_18.meaning: Who takes the NEXT step. Not who did the work; `owner` records that.
_next_action_by_vocabulary_2026_09_18.why_added: ADDED 2026-09-18. The `owner` field carries THREE different vocabularies - HUMAN, OWNER, COUNSEL, 'CLAUDE (proposal) then HUMAN (approval)' - and it means 'who did the work' in some rows and 'who does the next step' in others. An independent-review simulation filtering owner == HUMAN returned SEVEN blockers and MISSED B-017, which is one of the two production revocations. A registry is what a downstream consumer queries, so an ambiguous field there is a synchronization defect and not a style point. `owner` is left EXACTLY as it was, because it is the historical record of who was assigned. `next_action_by` is the unambiguous one: OWNER, COUNSEL, CLAUDE or NONE, and it answers only 'who takes the next step'.
